archetypes.name: test-stub-infra
archetypes.rationale: The three new convergence-streak test cases depend on per-round stub differentiation via LARCH_PLAN_REVIEW_*_SH overrides; the static panel does not verify whether the existing stub infrastructure can actually produce different round-by-round outputs as the plan assumes.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine `skills/design/scripts/test-plan-review-loop.sh` to determine whether the existing `LARCH_PLAN_REVIEW_DISPATCH_PANEL_SH`, `LARCH_PLAN_REVIEW_COLLECT_SH`, `LARCH_PLAN_REVIEW_TALLY_SH`, and `LARCH_PLAN_REVIEW_REVISE_SH` stub overrides support per-round differentiation — specifically whether a single stub script can produce different outputs for round 1 vs round 2 vs round 3 as the three proposed cases require. Verify whether existing `write_dispatch_*` helpers can emit the `ACCEPTED_COUNT`, `IMPORTANT_ACCEPTED_COUNT`, and `DEGRADED_PANEL` values that the plan's assertions target, and confirm that `round-summary.env` is written to the exact paths and contains the key names (`CONVERGENCE_STREAK`, `LOOP_STATUS`, `REASON`, `ROUNDS_COMPLETED`) the grep-based assertions expect. If the stub infrastructure cannot natively produce per-round branching, flag the plan as incomplete — it must specify how round-N differentiation is achieved inside a single overriding script. Also check whether the plan's optional fourth dedup unit test is scoped clearly enough to be implementable without ambiguity. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: orphan-reference
archetypes.rationale: The plan claims revise.env has no in-tree consumers based on an unspecified grep, but does not enumerate which files were checked; independent verification across docs, scripts, test fixtures, and comments is required before the allowlist removal can be treated as safe.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit all files under `scripts/`, `skills/`, and `docs/` for references to `revise.env` — including comments, grep-based test assertions, documentation prose, and variable assignments — to independently verify the plan's claim that no in-tree consumer of this file exists. Cross-check whether the allowlist enumerations in `scripts/lib-design-round-artifacts.md`, `skills/design/references/plan-review.md`, and `scripts/test-lib-design-round-artifacts.sh` are mutually consistent after the proposed edits, paying particular attention to the plan's assertion that line 39 of the test harness already pins `oos-accepted-design.md` without requiring a new assertion. Flag any reference to `revise.env` not accounted for by the plan, and flag any allowlist enumeration in one file that contradicts another's post-edit state. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
